answer: Swarms fail when each alias must ring a unique harbor buoy others cannot share. An applicant posts 4.05 POA and draws an 11-minute dawn circuit among 24 buoys. They clamp a 6.3 kg bronze clapper, then emit a 16-bit signal chirp bound to their pubkey and the epoch seed so the shore hydrophone records it in seconds 18-35. 150 clones would freeze 607.5 POA and need 150 exclusive buoys. Graders recompute the buoy draw from the seed, match the chirp to the hydrophone tape, and weigh the clapper to 30 g. A reused buoy, missed chirp, or bit collision cuts 51% and benches that circuit for 3 epochs.
